question: If a class-based dependency is listed in APIRouter(dependencies=[...]) and also declared as a parameter of the path operation, is the class instantiated once or twice per request?
reference_answer: If the same dependency is declared more than once for a path operation, FastAPI calls it only once per request. It caches the result and passes it to every dependant, unless you set use_cache=False. Router dependencies are added to every path operation of the router and run before the decorator and parameter dependencies. So by default the class is instantiated once per request.

question: Will a request with Content-Type: text/plain whose body is valid JSON still be parsed into my Pydantic body model, or is it rejected?
reference_answer: It is rejected. By default FastAPI checks Content-Type strictly for JSON bodies, and the body is parsed as JSON only with a valid JSON Content-Type such as application/json. This guards against CSRF attacks. strict_content_type=False only allows requests with no Content-Type header at all. The release notes add that before 0.65.2, text/plain requests containing JSON were accepted, and this was changed because text/plain requests skip CORS preflights.

question: Does pydantic-settings reread the .env file from disk every time I call Settings(), and how much does that actually cost per request if I don't wrap it in lru_cache?
reference_answer: Yes. Without lru_cache, each Settings() call creates a new object and reads the .env file again, so a new object is created and the file is read on every request. The docs describe reading a file from disk as usually costly (slow). With @lru_cache, Settings is created once on the first call and the same object is returned after that. The docs do not put a number on the cost per request.
